title: Ethiopia strengthens laboratory systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response - WHO | Regional Office for Africa

analysis.time: The project was initiated in 2024 and has been ongoing through 2026, with specific improvements noted between 2024 and 2025. The publication date is 2026-09-30.
analysis.location_and_population: Ethiopia, specifically focusing on its 27 laboratories established or upgraded since 2024, with efforts spanning 14 regions and involving over 22 million people in need of urgent assistance.
analysis.event: Ethiopia has strengthened its laboratory systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response, including the detection of priority infectious diseases such as Marburg virus disease, through a national multisectoral project supported by the Pandemic Fund and WHO. This is confirmed by the Ministry of Health and WHO.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The project has improved the detection of priority diseases, including Marburg virus disease, and reduced reporting errors by 90%. It has also enhanced molecular testing capacity at eight priority microbiology laboratories and trained over 1470 laboratory professionals. The scale of impact includes 27 laboratories, 41 AMR surveillance labs, and 267 health facilities in seven regions.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The project is ongoing, with laboratories now capable of conducting tests locally, reducing reliance on external facilities. The Ministry of Health has developed guidelines and SOPs, and over 40 facilities have received mentorship. The initiative is supported by the Pandemic Fund and WHO, with capacity assessments and equipment procurement completed in 2025.

analysis.brief_en: Ethiopia has been strengthening its laboratory systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response, particularly for priority infectious diseases like Marburg virus disease. This initiative, supported by the Pandemic Fund and the World Health Organization (WHO), includes the establishment and upgrading of 27 laboratories since 2024, with eight new microbiology labs for sentinel surveillance. The project has enhanced molecular testing capacity, reduced reporting errors by 90%, and trained over 1470 professionals in diagnostics, bioinformatics, and biosafety. Additionally, 267 health facilities in seven regions have procured transport vans to improve specimen delivery for testing. The Ministry of Health has developed standard operating procedures and guidelines, and over 40 facilities have received targeted mentorship. The initiative also includes the procurement of essential equipment, such as diagnostic tools and cold-chain systems, and the deployment of solar-powered refrigerators to veterinary clinics. These efforts aim to create a more integrated human and animal health response system, enabling faster and more accurate detection of outbreaks and improving public health outcomes.
analysis.summary_en: Ethiopia has been strengthening its laboratory systems to improve disease outbreak preparedness and response, particularly for priority infectious diseases like Marburg virus disease. This initiative, supported by the Pandemic Fund and the World Health Organization (WHO), includes the establishment and upgrading of 27 laboratories since 2024, with eight new microbiology labs for sentinel surveillance. The project has enhanced molecular testing capacity, reduced reporting errors by 90%, and trained over 1470 professionals in diagnostics, bioinformatics, and biosafety. Additionally, 267 health facilities in seven regions have procured transport vans to improve specimen delivery for testing. The Ministry of Health has developed standard operating procedures and guidelines, and over 40 facilities have received targeted mentorship. The initiative also includes the procurement of essential equipment, such as diagnostic tools and cold-chain systems, and the deployment of solar-powered refrigerators to veterinary clinics. These efforts aim to create a more integrated human and animal health response system, enabling faster and more accurate detection of outbreaks and improving public health outcomes.

title: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) Starts GMP Galidesivir Manufacturing for Ebola and Marburg Programs - Kalkine

analysis.time: Island Pharmaceuticals commenced GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir on 1 October 2026, with the first 5kg batch targeted for completion by the end of October and the second 5kg batch by late November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The first batch is earmarked for an approved emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak, while the second batch supports broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study.
analysis.event: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) has started GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir for its Ebola and Marburg development programs, with the first 5kg batch intended for an emergency-use program in Uganda and the second for broader development and a Marburg non-human primate study. This is confirmed by the company's announcement.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The production of 10kg of GMP API is planned, with the first 5kg batch aimed at near-term emergency-use requirements and the second for additional development activity. The program is intended to support potential outbreak deployment, future regulatory activity, and possible government procurement, but no efficacy outcomes are provided yet.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The manufacturing program includes analytical validation, reference-standard preparation, and stability studies to establish the quality framework for continued development. The emergency-use program will operate under the WHO's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions framework, and the Marburg program is being developed under the FDA Animal Rule. The company has not yet provided efficacy outcomes from the current emergency-use program.

analysis.brief_en: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) has initiated GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir for its Ebola and Marburg development programs. The first 5kg batch is expected to be completed by the end of October 2026 and is intended for an emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. A second 5kg batch is targeted for completion by late November 2026 to support broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The manufacturing program includes analytical validation, reference-standard preparation, and stability studies to establish the quality framework for continued development. The emergency-use program will operate under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions framework, while the Marburg program is being developed under the FDA Animal Rule. The company has not yet provided efficacy outcomes from the current emergency-use program, as treatment and data collection have not been completed. This marks a transition from preclinical work to physical production, with the aim of creating GMP-grade supply for clinical and regulatory programs.
analysis.summary_en: Island Pharmaceuticals Limited (ASX:ILA) has initiated GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir for its Ebola and Marburg development programs. The first 5kg batch is expected to be completed by the end of October 2026 and is intended for an emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. A second 5kg batch is targeted for completion by late November 2026 to support broader Ebola development and a pivotal Marburg non-human primate study. The manufacturing program includes analytical validation, reference-standard preparation, and stability studies to establish the quality framework for continued development. The emergency-use program will operate under the World Health Organization's Monitored Emergency Use of Unregistered and Investigational Interventions framework, while the Marburg program is being developed under the FDA Animal Rule. The company has not yet provided efficacy outcomes from the current emergency-use program, as treatment and data collection have not been completed. This marks a transition from preclinical work to physical production, with the aim of creating GMP-grade supply for clinical and regulatory programs.

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-10-02. Event date: 1 October 2026. The first 5kg batch is targeted for completion by the end of October 2026, and the second batch by late November 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: Uganda, with the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak affecting 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths as of 27 September 2026.
analysis.event: Island Pharmaceuticals commenced GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir API on 1 October 2026 at PI Health Sciences to support its emergency-use program in Uganda during the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak and its planned Marburg non-human primate study under the FDA Animal Rule.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The first 5kg batch is intended for the emergency-use program in Uganda, while the second 5kg batch will support broader Ebola strategy and the Marburg NHP study. The Bundibugyo outbreak has a confirmed case fatality ratio of approximately 48%. Galidesivir is authorised for investigational therapeutic use under the WHO MEURI framework.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The GMP manufacturing process is underway, with the first batch targeted for completion by the end of October 2026. The second batch is targeted for completion by late November 2026. The company will undertake finishing, vialing, and packaging activities before shipment to Uganda. The ongoing Bundibugyo outbreak is reported with confirmed case and death counts, but no specific treatment is currently approved.

analysis.brief_en: Island Pharmaceuticals has initiated GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir API at PI Health Sciences on 1 October 2026, supporting its emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. The first 5kg batch is expected to be completed by the end of October 2026, while the second 5kg batch will be ready by late November 2026 to aid broader Ebola strategies and a planned Marburg non-human primate study under the FDA Animal Rule. The Bundibugyo outbreak, as of 27 September 2026, has reported 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths, with a case fatality ratio of about 48%. Galidesivir is authorized for investigational use under the WHO MEURI framework, allowing data collection on clinical, safety, and virological outcomes. No approved specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, highlighting the significance of this development. The company will complete finishing, vialing, and packaging before shipment to Uganda. This action is part of a larger program including analytical method validation, reference standard preparation, and stability studies to support Galidesivir's development and potential regulatory procurement.
analysis.summary_en: Island Pharmaceuticals has initiated GMP manufacturing of Galidesivir API at PI Health Sciences on 1 October 2026, supporting its emergency-use program in Uganda during the ongoing Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak. The first 5kg batch is expected to be completed by the end of October 2026, while the second 5kg batch will be ready by late November 2026 to aid broader Ebola strategies and a planned Marburg non-human primate study under the FDA Animal Rule. The Bundibugyo outbreak, as of 27 September 2026, has reported 8,137 confirmed cases and 3,926 confirmed deaths, with a case fatality ratio of about 48%. Galidesivir is authorized for investigational use under the WHO MEURI framework, allowing data collection on clinical, safety, and virological outcomes. No approved specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease, highlighting the significance of this development. The company will complete finishing, vialing, and packaging before shipment to Uganda. This action is part of a larger program including analytical method validation, reference standard preparation, and stability studies to support Galidesivir's development and potential regulatory procurement.
